policy_prompt_for_subgoal: The number of required pick-ups comes from the goal instruction: 'pick up ... again' means 1 pick-up; 'for two times' means 2 pick-ups; 'three times' means 3 pick-ups. An episode starts in subgoal A: pick up the cube, pointing at the cube the demonstration grasped. The point for A is never taken from memory; it is found from what the step shows, by the point rule at the end of this instruction. The memory holds only picks_done. Rules, applied at every decision step after updating memory: - The robot is holding the cube if and only if the scene at this decision step shows the gripper raised (height about 0.12 or more) with fingers partly closed (about 46-51%, not 100%); the cube list is irrelevant to this test (the held cube may still be listed at its old table position), and fingers 100% open means not holding regardless of any 'lifted off the table' line. Holding: choose B: put it down. - Otherwise (fingers 100% open): if picks_done is less than the required number of pick-ups, choose A: pick up the cube, pointing at the cube given by the point rule below; if picks_done equals or exceeds the required number, choose C: press the button to finish. Point rule for A. At the first decision step (memory empty), use the demonstration steps shown at that step: find the demonstration frame where the gripper is lowest (height about 0.02) with fingers about 46-51% open; the grasped cube is the listed cube (from a demonstration frame before the gripper descended) nearest that gripper position, and it is the cube reported 'held in the gripper' in the following frames. Ignore cubes that vanish from the list earlier while the gripper is high and 100% open; they are only hidden by the arm. After the demonstration's put-down, follow that cube through every remaining demonstration frame: in each frame it is the listed cube nearest its position in the previous frame (cubes swap places during the shuffle and move tens of pixels per frame, and lists are sorted by y, not identity; do not assume it returns to its old spot). Point at the cube in the scene at the start of execution nearest its last demonstration position. At every later decision step where A is chosen, the execution steps shown contain the put-down descent: the frame where the gripper is at table height (below about 0.04) with the fingers opening; point at the listed cube in the scene at this decision step (the last frame shown) nearest that descent position, since that is the cube just set down and the cube to pick again. Pointing at the listed cube position, or within a few px of it (such as the demonstration's grasp position), is acceptable. Never point at any other cube.

fields.name: picks_done
fields.description: Count of completed pick-ups. Write 0 at the first decision step (memory empty). At any later step, look only at the gripper in the last frame shown (the scene at this decision step): if it is raised (height about 0.12 or more) with fingers partly closed (about 46-51%, not 100%), write the carried value plus one, no matter what the cube list says (the held cube may still be listed at its old table position); if the fingers are 100% open, copy the carried value unchanged even if a cube line says 'lifted off the table'. e.g. 1
